research.name: AdaptOrch: Task-Adaptive Multi-Agent Orchestration
research.description: Task-adaptive orchestration that maps decomposition shape to execution pattern instead of using one static topology

research.name: Latency-Aware Orchestration for Parallel Multi-Agent Systems
research.description: Accuracy and latency tradeoffs for parallel execution modeled over probabilistic DAGs

research.name: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Orchestration
research.description: Dynamic sequencing and prioritization with a learned orchestrator, useful as a design reference not a direct recipe

research.name: Aligned Agents, Biased Swarm: Measuring Bias Amplification in Multi-Agent Systems (Li et al., ICLR 2026)
research.description: Peer-reviewed (ICLR 2026, open code). Structured multi-agent workflows amplify individual-agent bias into systemic polarization; injecting neutral context can accelerate it. Basis for the structured-pipeline bias anti-pattern.

research.name: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets (Tran & Kiela)
research.description: Apr 2026 arXiv preprint, NOT peer-reviewed; scope limited to multi-hop reasoning, text-only. Data Processing Inequality argument for single-agent superiority at equal budget. Basis for the equal-budget fan-out trap. Verify before relying.

research.name: Agent Contracts: A Formal Framework for Resource-Bounded Autonomous AI Systems (Ye & Tan)
research.description: 2026 arXiv paper establishing the budget-conservation invariant (child agent budgets are strict subsets of the parent's remaining budget) cited in SKILL.md §Operating Principles for per-worker budget enforcement.

community_resources.name: figaro

community_resources.name: gstack
community_resources.description: Claude Code configured as a virtual engineering team; reference for role-based agent orchestration and parallel workstreams

community_resources.name: LangGraph
community_resources.description: Agents-as-graphs framework for multi-agent orchestration with explicit state management; 26.8k stars, strong reference for DAG-based orchestration patterns

community_resources.name: Codex Multi Agent Playbook (am.will)
community_resources.description: Secondary inspiration for Codex swarm workflows; useful for examples but should be checked against primary docs

community_resources.name: CODEX MULTI AGENT PLAYBOOK: SWARMS LVL. 1 (@LLMJunky)
community_resources.description: Long-form X Article on multi-agent swarm orchestration with Codex — covers Swarm Waves (sequential parallelism), Super Swarms (total parallelism), orchestrator roles, dependency graphs, max_threads config, and model/reasoning level selection per agent

community_resources.name: Nav Toor — 30 Claude Code Sub-Agents I Actually Use
community_resources.description: Practitioner catalog of 30 sub-agent .md definitions across 8 categories (2026-05-01; 96K views). Cited narrowly for the 'Worker Self-Rejection Rules' section: the cross-cutting pattern of embedding a named negative criterion ('reject your own draft if X') in worker system prompts to pre-filter plausible-but-wrong output before it reaches the lead. The 30-agent catalog itself is a prompt-template reference, not absorbed piecemeal; the self-rejection rule is the load-bearing design pattern lifted from it.

community_resources.name: Claude Subagents vs. Agent Teams, Explained (@akshay_pachaar)
community_resources.description: Explainer on two distinct multi-agent paradigms in Claude Code: when to use subagents (isolated context, delegation) vs. agent teams (collaborative, shared context). Key insight: most people reach for multi-agent when they shouldn't

community_resources.name: The Machine that Builds the Machine — Symphony (@daniel_mac8)
community_resources.description: Deep dive on OpenAI's Symphony — an Elixir-based orchestrator that polls Linear, spawns Codex agents in isolated workspaces, implements features, self-reviews PRs, and manages full issue lifecycle. Real numbers: 26 tasks, 27 PRs, 32K LOC in 36 hours at 10-agent concurrency

community_resources.name: Andrej Karpathy - Claude Coding Notes
community_resources.description: Operator-level coding-agent pitfalls that justify verifier loops, tighter scope control, and resistance to overcomplicated multi-agent execution

community_resources.name: Sarah Chieng - Lessons Learned From Building Multi-Agent Workflows
community_resources.description: April 2026 field report on orchestrator-plus-line-cook patterns, minimum viable context, phased fan-out, no shared-file writes, and one-builder-plus-verifiers discipline

community_resources.name: Walden Yan - Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working
community_resources.description: April 2026 Cognition update: parallel-writer swarms still fail in practice; the narrow class that works is manager-and-workers setups where extra agents contribute intelligence while writes stay single-threaded

community_resources.name: Claude Code Agents In 2026: Agent View, Subagents, Teams, And What Parallel Sessions Actually Cost
community_resources.description: June 2026 cost analysis: tiered-model teams (Opus lead + Sonnet workers + Haiku formatters) cost ~40% less than all-Opus at minimal capability loss. Also covers /clear between dispatches cutting per-message token cost 30–50%.

community_resources.name: Agentic AI Frameworks 2026: LangGraph vs CrewAI vs OpenAI SDK
community_resources.description: June 2026 framework landscape: Microsoft merged AutoGen + Semantic Kernel into Microsoft Agent Framework v1.0 (GA April 2026) — AutoGen is now in maintenance mode. OpenAI Agents SDK April 2026 overhaul added native sandbox, sub-agent patterns, and first-class MCP. Used as basis for Framework Quick-Pick table in SKILL.md.

community_resources.name: Multi-Agent in Production 2026: 3 Patterns That Survived
community_resources.description: May 2026 production survey describing orchestrator-worker as the default multi-agent pattern in production, alongside supervisor/hierarchical and swarm (peer, no central control) as the other two topologies that survived. The page does not state a specific adoption percentage — do not cite a numeric split from this source.
